a.text: Úlfhildur's mother tongue is Icelandic.

b.text: Úlfhildur grew up speaking Danish as her first language.

label: contradiction
reason: One gives Icelandic as Úlfhildur's mother tongue, the other says she grew up with Danish as her native language.

a.text: Since spring, Haitham gets around the old town on shared e-bikes.

b.text: In the new business district Haitham takes the metro between meetings.

label: non_contradiction
reason: E-bikes in the old town and the metro in the business district belong to different parts of the city, so both habits fit.

a.text: Gunārs has one boxing coach: his old schoolteacher.

b.text: A retired ferry captain is Gunārs's boxing coach.

label: contradiction
reason: Gunārs's boxing coach is his old schoolteacher in one and a retired ferry captain in the other.

a.text: Wilfredo only learned to sail at forty, on a weekend course at the bay.

b.text: As a boy, Wilfredo crewed his grandfather's dinghy every summer, handling the jib.

label: contradiction
reason: Learning to sail at forty does not fit with crewing a dinghy every summer as a boy.

a.text: Lihong passed the driving test as a teenager, on the very first try.

b.text: Lihong got a driving licence at seventeen.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Seventeen is a teenage age, so passing as a teenager and being licensed at seventeen agree.

a.text: Niruta's scholarship application is due in March.

b.text: Niruta's scholarship interview is in March.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Sending in the application and sitting the interview are separate steps, and both can fall in March for Niruta.

a.text: Rebwar teaches a calligraphy class at the cultural centre on Saturdays.

b.text: Rebwar now teaches the calligraphy class on Sundays instead of Saturdays, as the hall is booked for weddings.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The newer memory says Rebwar's calligraphy class has gone from Saturdays to Sundays.

a.text: Rasmané wears one silver bracelet, a gift from his aunt.

b.text: The only bracelet Rasmané wears, a silver one, came from his godmother.

label: contradiction
reason: Rasmané's single silver bracelet is said to come from his aunt and from his godmother.

a.text: Darshan flies his kites on the dunes on windy afternoons.

b.text: Darshan flies kites on the school field during the kite festival in the holidays.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Kite flying on the dunes on windy afternoons and on the school field at the festival are different occasions that both fit.

a.text: Thongsavath has never had a job interview.

b.text: Three managers sat across the table from Thongsavath when he was interviewed for his post at the rice mill.

label: contradiction
reason: Being interviewed by three managers for his post clashes with Thongsavath never having had a job interview.

a.text: Brishti's first job was sweeping floors and folding rugs at a carpet shop.

b.text: Brishti's very first job was waiting tables at a café near her college.

label: contradiction
reason: Two different jobs are each named as the earliest one Brishti ever had.

a.text: Bhagya is embroidering a silk table runner as a housewarming gift.

b.text: Bhagya has been stitching peacocks onto a silk table runner since July, for a friend's housewarming.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Both describe Bhagya's housewarming table runner, and one adds the peacocks and when she began it.

a.text: The piece Sandi will play at the end-of-term recital lasts seven minutes.

b.text: Sandi's end-of-term recital piece runs to nine minutes.

label: contradiction
reason: One recital piece has one length, given as seven minutes and as nine.

a.text: Yorleny's rent falls due on the first of each month.

b.text: Yorleny pays her rent on the fifth of every month, the day it falls due.

label: contradiction
reason: Yorleny's monthly rent is due on the 1st by one account and on the 5th by the other.

a.text: Three hundred guests were invited to the wedding of Tesfit's daughter.

b.text: Tesfit's daughter's wedding had four hundred invited guests.

label: contradiction
reason: The same wedding has three hundred invited guests in one memory and four hundred in the other.

a.text: Nokwanda listens to classical music while she paints.

b.text: While painting, Nokwanda plays baroque harpsichord pieces.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Baroque harpsichord pieces are classical music, so one names the music Nokwanda paints to.

a.text: Hiske's favourite smell is rain on dry dust.

b.text: Hiske's favourite sound is rain on the roof.

label: non_contradiction
reason: A favourite smell and a favourite sound are different facts, so both can be true.

a.text: Every night Dela cooks supper for eight.

b.text: Dela's nightly supper pot feeds two adults and six children.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Two adults and six children make eight, so both give the same size for Dela's nightly supper.

a.text: Cesira has five exams in her final session at university.

b.text: Six exams make up Cesira's final session at university.

label: contradiction
reason: Cesira's final exam session holds five exams in one memory and six in the other.

a.text: Diaraye ran the anchor leg for her team at the river relay.

b.text: At the river relay, Diaraye took the baton for the final leg and brought her team home.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The anchor leg of a relay is its final leg, so both describe the same run by Diaraye.

a.text: The well in Alan's courtyard is twelve metres deep.

b.text: Alan's courtyard well goes down twenty metres.

label: contradiction
reason: Alan's courtyard well is twelve metres deep according to one and twenty according to the other.

a.text: Vígþór has never handled money at work.

b.text: Each evening Vígþór counts the café's till and carries the day's takings to the bank.

label: contradiction
reason: Counting the till and banking the takings is handling money, which Vígþór supposedly never does at work.

a.text: Last week Shoumik moved his coin jar from the kitchen shelf to his bedroom.

b.text: Shoumik moved the coin jar last week, out of his bedroom and onto the kitchen shelf.

label: contradiction
reason: The same move of Shoumik's coin jar last week is told in opposite directions.

a.text: Sena meets friends at the café in the train station.

b.text: Sena works weekend shifts at the newsstand in the train station.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Meeting friends at the station café and working at the station newsstand are separate facts that fit.

a.text: Bergþór's car has no roof rack.

b.text: Every winter weekend Bergþór straps the skis to the roof rack of the car.

label: contradiction
reason: A car with no roof rack clashes with skis strapped to that car's roof rack.

a.text: Mebrahtu's short film won the audience award at the city festival.

b.text: At the city festival, the audience voted Mebrahtu's short film their favourite.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Winning the audience award is the audience voting the film its favourite, so both say the same of Mebrahtu's film.

a.text: Idowu stopped buying bottled water two years ago.

b.text: Idowu hasn't bought a plastic bottle of water since 2023.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Giving up bottled water two years ago matches buying none in the years after, so both describe one habit.

a.text: Sukhleen rents her flat fully furnished.

b.text: Sukhleen's flat came empty, and every piece of furniture in it is her own.

label: contradiction
reason: A flat rented fully furnished clashes with one that came empty and holds only Sukhleen's furniture.

a.text: Man-Yee's daughter plays with her cousin in the courtyard every evening.

b.text: Man-Yee's daughter's cousin moved to another city, so now the girls only see each other on video calls.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The newer memory says the cousin moved away, so the evening play is only on video calls.

a.text: Yendry studies in the faculty library on weekday mornings.

b.text: At weekends Yendry revises at a café near the train station.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Weekday mornings in the library and weekends at a station café are separate study habits of Yendry's.

a.text: Assitan's bus to work stops right by the bakery.

b.text: Since the roadworks began, Assitan's bus stops by the post office instead of the bakery.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The newer memory says the roadworks put Assitan's stop by the post office in place of the bakery.

a.text: Osei's wife's family comes from a fishing town on the coast.

b.text: Osei's in-laws come from a farming village in the far north.

label: contradiction
reason: The coast and a farming village in the far north are given as the home of the same family of Osei's wife.

a.text: Mahluga sells tickets at the cinema's box office.

b.text: Mahluga took over the cinema's projection booth in spring, when the old projectionist retired, and left the box office to a student.

label: non_contradiction
reason: In the newer memory Mahluga runs the projection booth, having handed the box office to a student.

a.text: Urmas tutors two secondary school students in physics.

b.text: Urmas took on a third physics student in February, so he tutors three in all.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Taking on a third pupil brought Urmas up to three physics students, according to the newer memory.

a.text: Radosław sleeps in total darkness, with blackout curtains and no lights.

b.text: Radosław always leaves a small nightlight on in the bedroom.

label: contradiction
reason: Total darkness at night clashes with always leaving a nightlight on.

a.text: Apeksha's house has no water heater, so she warms her bath water on the stove.

b.text: Apeksha takes hot showers from the electric heater fixed above her bathroom tap.

label: contradiction
reason: A house with no water heater clashes with Apeksha showering from an electric heater in her bathroom.

a.text: Manveer is training for his first 10K, with three short runs a week.

b.text: Manveer ran his first 10K in February and has entered a full marathon for the autumn.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The newer memory says Manveer has done the 10K he was training for and is aiming at a marathon.

a.text: There is no electricity at all in Dahti's cabin.

b.text: Every night Dahti charges the phone from the kitchen socket in the cabin.

label: contradiction
reason: A cabin with no electricity cannot have a working kitchen socket for charging a phone.

a.text: Chiyo's neighbourhood sewing circle meets once a week, on Thursdays.

b.text: Chiyo's neighbourhood sewing circle meets every Wednesday afternoon.

label: contradiction
reason: The weekly meeting day of Chiyo's sewing circle is Thursday in one memory and Wednesday in the other.

a.text: Kulthida never carries cash; she pays for everything by scanning a code on her phone.

b.text: At the morning market, Kulthida counts out notes and coins from her purse for the vegetables.

label: contradiction
reason: Paying with notes and coins from her purse means Kulthida carries cash, which she is said never to do.

a.text: Apolonia knits all her jumpers by hand.

b.text: Apolonia bought a knitting machine in the spring and turns out her jumpers on it these days.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Apolonia's jumpers come off a knitting machine bought in spring, the newer memory says, not from hand knitting.

a.text: Hawi runs her own tailoring shop and has no boss.

b.text: Hawi reports to a floor manager at the garment factory where she sews all week.

label: contradiction
reason: Having no boss and running her own shop clashes with Hawi reporting to a factory floor manager.

a.text: Jaldessa's cow calved on Tuesday night.

b.text: It was on Wednesday night that Jaldessa's cow calved.

label: contradiction
reason: The single calving is placed on Tuesday night by one memory and Wednesday night by the other.

a.text: Not once has Babatope eaten a meal in a restaurant.

b.text: Babatope has a regular table at the fish restaurant by the harbour and eats there most weeks.

label: contradiction
reason: A regular restaurant table does not fit with Babatope never having eaten in a restaurant.

a.text: Ngari writes in a travel journal on every trip.

b.text: Ngari keeps a handwritten travel journal with bus and train ticket stubs glued between the pages.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Ngari's travel journal appears in each, and one adds that it is handwritten with ticket stubs.

a.text: Isha has never taught a class in her life.

b.text: Every evening Isha marks her pupils' homework, and each spring she takes her class on the school trip.

label: contradiction
reason: Marking her pupils' homework and taking her class on trips means Isha teaches, which the other memory denies.

a.text: Mikel's flat is above a bakery.

b.text: Mikel wakes each morning to the smell of bread baking in the shop on the ground floor below him.

label: non_contradiction
reason: A bread shop on the ground floor below Mikel is the bakery his flat sits above, so both agree.

a.text: Kaspar's band plays only covers of old rock songs at village fêtes.

b.text: Kaspar's band no longer plays covers; since the summer they perform only songs Kaspar and the singer wrote.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Covers are out for Kaspar's band in the newer memory, which has it playing only its own songs.

a.text: Shno always spends New Year's Eve at home with her family.

b.text: Shno spent last New Year's Eve abroad with friends, watching fireworks from a bridge.

label: contradiction
reason: Always being home with family on New Year's Eve clashes with spending the last one abroad with friends.

a.text: Hemanta built a wooden kennel for the dog.

b.text: Hemanta built a wooden coop for the hens.

label: non_contradiction
reason: A kennel for the dog and a coop for the hens are two different things Hemanta built, so both fit.

a.text: Volkan reads aloud to his nephew at bedtime when he babysits.

b.text: During the school holidays Volkan reads stories aloud at the library's story hour.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Reading to a nephew at bedtime and reading at the library story hour are separate occasions, with no exclusive word.

a.text: Adebimpe has not missed a single school day this school year.

b.text: This school year, Adebimpe missed a full week of lessons in October for her cousin's wedding.

label: contradiction
reason: A missed week of lessons in October cannot fit with Adebimpe's perfect attendance over the same school year.

a.text: Desi's son goes to his grandparents' house after school on Mondays.

b.text: Desi's son spends Thursday afternoons after school at his aunt's.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Mondays at the grandparents' and Thursdays at the aunt's are different days of after-school care, so there is no clash.

a.text: The head of Kakooza's drum is made of cowhide.

b.text: Kakooza has a single drum, and its head is goatskin.

label: contradiction
reason: Kakooza's one drum has a cowhide head in one account and a goatskin head in the other.

a.text: Gudmund whistles while shovelling snow in the mornings.

b.text: On Saturday drives Gudmund sings along to the car radio.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Whistling at morning snow-shovelling and singing on Saturday drives are different times and fit together.

a.text: Kesinee volunteers at the river clean-up on Saturday mornings.

b.text: On Wednesday evenings Kesinee helps out at the seniors' centre, serving tea and running bingo.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Volunteering at two places on different days fits together, with no word making either exclusive.

a.text: On sunny days Siiri hangs the laundry on the flat roof.

b.text: On rainy days Siiri hangs the laundry on a rack in the bathroom.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Drying laundry on the roof in sun and in the bathroom in rain are habits for different weather.

a.text: Sekou never sat the national university entrance exam.

b.text: Sekou scored in the top thousand of the whole country on the national university entrance exam.

label: contradiction
reason: Never having sat the national entrance exam cannot fit with scoring in its top thousand, as the other memory says of Sekou.

a.text: Lokelani snacks on roasted chickpeas at work.

b.text: In the afternoons Lokelani snacks on roasted chickpeas sprinkled with chilli salt at her desk.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Lokelani's roasted chickpea snack at work gains chilli salt and an afternoon time in one telling.

a.text: Amarjot keeps a jar of old train tickets on the bookshelf.

b.text: Amarjot keeps a jar of seashells from different beaches on the bookshelf.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Old train tickets and seashells are two different jars, and a shelf can hold both.

a.text: Elin's kayak paddle has been hanging in the boathouse shed since spring.

b.text: Elin's kayak has been resting on trestles in the boathouse shed since spring.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Where Elin's paddle hangs and where the kayak rests are two separate facts about gear in the same shed.

a.text: Vanhxay started as a line cook at the riverside hotel and was later promoted to head chef.

b.text: Vanhxay began as a line cook at the riverside hotel; later he was promoted, but only to pastry chef, never head chef.

label: contradiction
reason: The accounts of Vanhxay's one promotion at the riverside hotel disagree: head chef in one, pastry chef and never head chef in the other.

a.text: Ludmila's only zither has ten strings.

b.text: Ludmila plays her one small folk zither, an old instrument with eleven strings.

label: contradiction
reason: Ludmila has a single zither, and its string count is ten in one account and eleven in the other.

a.text: Manana makes her breakfast porridge only from cornmeal.

b.text: Manana's breakfast porridge is made only from buckwheat.

label: contradiction
reason: With the word only on both sides, cornmeal and buckwheat cannot each be the sole grain of Manana's porridge.

a.text: Hawre teaches at a primary school in the old quarter.

b.text: After the summer, Hawre took up a lecturer post at the teacher training college and left his primary school class.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The newer memory says Hawre left primary teaching for a lecturer post at the training college.

a.text: The film society Huenu runs now holds its screenings in the old school hall.

b.text: Huenu's film society now screens its films in the back room of the café.

label: contradiction
reason: Both describe where Huenu's film society screens at present, and they name two different places.

a.text: Iria took the cover photo for her own novel, a foggy shot of the estuary.

b.text: The cover photo on Iria's novel was taken by her brother.

label: contradiction
reason: Only one person took the cover photo on Iria's novel, and the two name Iria and her brother.

a.text: Altagracia's play has three acts.

b.text: Altagracia wrote her play in an opening act, a middle act and a closing act.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Opening, middle and closing acts make three, matching the act count of Altagracia's play.

a.text: Urška has lived in her hometown all her life.

b.text: Urška worked abroad for ten years before going back to her hometown.

label: contradiction
reason: Ten years working abroad clashes with having lived in her hometown all her life.

a.text: Nargiz studied engineering in the capital.

b.text: Nargiz did her engineering degree in a small university town in the east.

label: contradiction
reason: The engineering studies are placed in the capital in one account and in a small eastern town in the other.

a.text: Ngaire stopped going to her school reunions after the 2015 one.

b.text: Ngaire has organised every school reunion since 2015.

label: contradiction
reason: Giving up school reunions after a given year clashes with organising every reunion since that same year.

a.text: Eilev spends most weekends photographing weddings in the fjord villages around his town.

b.text: Over the winter Eilev gave up wedding jobs, and he shoots portraits in a small studio above the hardware shop instead.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The newer memory says Eilev gave up wedding work over the winter in favour of studio portraits.

a.text: This month Lesbia replaced the canary that flew off with a pair of finches.

b.text: Lesbia replaced the escaped canary this month with another canary from the market.

label: contradiction
reason: The bird that took the lost canary's place is a pair of finches in one account and a new canary in the other.

a.text: Hinewai does yoga in the evenings.

b.text: Each evening Hinewai unrolls her mat by the woodstove for forty minutes of slow yoga poses.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Forty minutes on the mat by the woodstove each evening fills in Hinewai's evening yoga.

a.text: Natela grabs a banana after every run; it is her go-to snack.

b.text: Natela always reaches for a rice ball after running.

label: contradiction
reason: Natela's usual snack after running is a banana in one account and always a rice ball in the other.

a.text: Qusai rents a single room in a shared compound near the bakery.

b.text: Qusai finished building his own house last year and lives in it.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Qusai's newer memory has him living in the house he built, not a rented compound room.

a.text: Tamrat never goes out on the lake.

b.text: Tamrat paddles a canoe across the lake to the island market.

label: contradiction
reason: Paddling across the lake means going out on it, which clashes with never doing so.

a.text: Noy's in-laws have never set foot in her home.

b.text: Noy's mother-in-law stayed with her for the whole of last winter.

label: contradiction
reason: If Noy's mother-in-law spent a winter in her home, the in-laws cannot have never set foot there.

a.text: On his birthday, Tangi stopped at the rink and skated for an hour.

b.text: Tangi stopped at the rink on his birthday but never put on skates, just watched.

label: contradiction
reason: The birthday visit to the rink has Tangi skating an hour in one and never skating in the other.

a.text: Azadeh can hold a plank for three minutes.

b.text: Azadeh can hold a side plank for three minutes.

label: non_contradiction
reason: A plank and a side plank are different exercises, so both holds can be true for Azadeh.

a.text: On his last trip Manouchehr spent seven nights at the mountain guesthouse.

b.text: Manouchehr's last stay at the mountain guesthouse lasted nine nights.

label: contradiction
reason: The same last stay at the guesthouse is seven nights in one account and nine in the other.

a.text: Grażyna plays on the Tuesday quiz team at the pub on the corner.

b.text: Grażyna switched to the Thursday quiz team at the hotel bar and no longer plays on Tuesdays.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The newer memory says Grażyna left the Tuesday pub quiz for the Thursday hotel quiz.

a.text: Guðrið's aunt rows in the village boat team.

b.text: Guðrið's aunt coaches the village boat team.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Rowing in the team and coaching it are two different roles the aunt can hold at once.

a.text: Every new year, Brais's grandmother cooks the big family feast.

b.text: Brais took over cooking the family's new-year feast last year, giving his grandmother a rest.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The newer memory says Brais has taken the new-year feast over from his grandmother.

a.text: Linen is the fabric Harika loves most.

b.text: Harika would pick wool over any other fabric, every time.

label: contradiction
reason: Harika's most loved fabric is linen in one memory and wool in the other, with no change in the words.

a.text: Siavash goes to the market twice a week.

b.text: Every Tuesday and Friday, Siavash walks to the market with his cloth bags.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Tuesday and Friday are two days, which is the same as going twice a week.

a.text: Shwetha dusts the bookshelves on weekday evenings.

b.text: Shwetha dusts the ceiling fans on Sunday mornings.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Bookshelves on weekday evenings and ceiling fans on Sunday mornings are separate dusting habits.

a.text: Roudabeh hits a two-handed backhand.

b.text: Roudabeh switched to a one-handed backhand in August after her coach suggested it.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The newer memory says Roudabeh changed her two-handed backhand to a one-handed one.

a.text: Ulviyya never uses an alarm clock and wakes on her own at dawn.

b.text: Two alarm clocks ring on Ulviyya's nightstand every morning, five minutes apart.

label: contradiction
reason: Never using an alarm clock clashes with two of them ringing beside her each morning.

a.text: Since the office relocated, Sum-Yi rides the metro to work every day.

b.text: Since the office relocated, Sum-Yi walks to work every day; it is only ten minutes from her flat.

label: contradiction
reason: Riding the metro daily and walking daily are two different answers for how Sum-Yi gets to the relocated office.

a.text: Ritwik has all his shirts stitched by a tailor in the old bazaar.

b.text: Ritwik now buys ready-made shirts off the rack instead of having them stitched by a tailor.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The newer memory says Ritwik buys ready-made shirts rather than tailored ones.

a.text: Aurelia takes her grandson to football practice.

b.text: On Saturdays Aurelia carries her grandson to football practice on the back of her scooter.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Both tell of Aurelia taking her grandson to football practice; one adds the day and the scooter.

a.text: Cleiton feeds the street dogs near his building in the mornings.

b.text: On Sunday evenings Cleiton brings a bag of food for the stray dogs at the bus depot.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Morning feeding near his building and Sunday evening feeding at the depot are different times and places, so both hold.

a.text: Chiman has never owned a smartphone and still uses a small flip phone.

b.text: Every evening Chiman scrolls through photos of the grandchildren on a smartphone with a cracked corner.

label: contradiction
reason: Never owning a smartphone clashes with scrolling on one every evening; a borrowed phone would be an invented escape.

a.text: Umuhoza catches rainwater in buckets set under the edge of the roof.

b.text: Umuhoza now has a gutter feeding rainwater into a big tank, so the buckets are put away.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Buckets under the roof edge gave way to a gutter and tank, which the newer memory states.

a.text: Jithin has never seen a ballet performed live.

b.text: Jithin watched a ballet from the balcony of the city theatre last winter, sitting beside his niece.

label: contradiction
reason: Watching a ballet from a theatre balcony is seeing one live, which Jithin is said never to have done.

a.text: For the school run, Fabiola switched from the family car to a cargo bike.

b.text: Fabiola switched from the bus to a cargo bike for the school run.

label: contradiction
reason: The one switch to a cargo bike is made from the family car in one account and from the bus in the other.

a.text: Eleonora's grandmother never learned to read.

b.text: Each morning Eleonora's grandmother reads the newspaper aloud to the whole kitchen.

label: contradiction
reason: Someone who never learned to read could not read the newspaper aloud every morning.

a.text: Nomakhosazana shares her flat with a flatmate from work.

b.text: Nomakhosazana's flatmate packed up over the new year, so she has the flat to herself these days.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Nomakhosazana's flatmate packed up over the new year, which the newer memory gives as the change.

a.text: Ditlev hangs his laundry on the line in the yard.

b.text: Ditlev now dries his laundry in the machine at the new flat instead of on the line.

label: non_contradiction
reason: The newer memory says Ditlev uses a dryer at the new flat instead of the line.

a.text: Lirie dries figs on the flat roof in August.

b.text: Lirie dries peppers on the flat roof in August.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Figs and peppers can both be drying on the roof, so these are separate facts.

a.text: Raghavendra has no fridge in his flat and buys vegetables fresh each day.

b.text: Raghavendra chills bottles of buttermilk in his fridge for when guests drop by.

label: contradiction
reason: One says Raghavendra's flat has no fridge, while the other has him chilling buttermilk in his fridge.

a.text: Aristide had the roof fixed first and the walls painted later.

b.text: Aristide had the walls painted before anything else, and the roof was fixed later that autumn.

label: contradiction
reason: The order of Aristide's roof repair and wall painting is reversed between the two accounts.

a.text: Ayotunde is training to be a sign language interpreter.

b.text: Ayotunde is training to be a sign language interpreter on an evening course, in its second year.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Ayotunde's training as a sign language interpreter appears in each; one adds that it is an evening course already a year along.

a.text: Nima can't bear anything sour.

b.text: Nima snacks on unripe green plums dipped in salt.

label: contradiction
reason: Unripe green plums are very sour, so snacking on them clashes with Nima not bearing sour food.

a.text: Aoko's dog gets 300 grams of food a day.

b.text: Aoko feeds her dog 150 grams in the morning and 150 grams in the evening.

label: non_contradiction
reason: Two meals of 150 grams add up to the same 300 grams a day.

a.text: Ragnvald sells spices from a stall at the Friday market.

b.text: On Sundays Ragnvald runs his spice stall at the harbour market.
